pharm: Fluoroquinolone; inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase & topoisomerase IV
summary: Broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic for respiratory, urinary, skin and other infections. Carries a boxed warning for disabling, potentially irreversible tendon, nerve and CNS reactions; reserve for uncomplicated infections only when no alternative exists.
indications: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis (reserve use)

dosage.n: Combine with anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam if Pseudomonas
Or 500 mg q24h x 10-14 days; reserve use
See label tables for CrCl-based dosing

admin: Tablets to pediatric patients weighing >=30 kg only
Take at least 2 hours before or after antacids, iron, zinc, sucralfate, multivitamins or didanosine
May be taken with or without food
Maintain adequate hydration to avoid crystalluria
Complete full course; do not stop early
moa: Bactericidal fluoroquinolone that inhibits bacterial topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase) and topoisomerase IV, enzymes required for bacterial DNA replication, transcription, repair and recombination.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to levofloxacin or other quinolones
relative: History of myasthenia gravis (avoid — may worsen muscle weakness)
Known QT prolongation, uncorrected hypokalemia, or concomitant QT-prolonging drugs
History of tendon disorders or prior fluoroquinolone-associated serious reaction
monitor: Tendon pain/swelling — stop immediately if suspected
Blood glucose in diabetics on hypoglycemic agents
CNS effects and peripheral neuropathy symptoms

preg: Category C — use only if potential benefit justifies fetal risk; no adequate controlled human studies.
lact: Presumed excreted in human milk; weigh discontinuing nursing vs drug due to risk to infant.
renal: Adjust dose when CrCl <50 mL/min; not efficiently removed by hemo- or peritoneal dialysis.
hepatic: No routine adjustment; discontinue immediately if signs of hepatitis (severe, sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity reported).

major: QT-prolonging drugs (class IA/III antiarrhythmics, TCAs, macrolides, antipsychotics) — additive torsades risk
Warfarin — enhanced anticoagulant effect; monitor INR/bleeding
Antidiabetic agents (insulin, sulfonylureas) — hypo/hyperglycemia, careful glucose monitoring
moderate: Multivalent cations (antacids, iron, zinc, sucralfate, multivitamins, didanosine) — reduced absorption
NSAIDs — may increase CNS stimulation/seizure risk
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; may add to CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May produce false-positive opiate urine screens (class effect).

emergency: Anaphylaxis or serious skin reaction (occasionally fatal, may occur after first dose) — seek emergency care
Sudden severe chest, back or abdominal pain (possible aortic dissection)
Tendon pain/snap/swelling — stop drug, rest limb, seek care
New numbness/tingling/weakness, seizures, or severe mood/behavior changes

monitoring: Signs of tendinitis/tendon rupture (especially >60 yrs, on steroids, transplant patients)
Renal function and hydration; LFTs if hepatic symptoms
counsel: Stop and call your doctor at first sign of tendon pain, swelling or a snap
Report numbness, tingling, weakness, mood changes or seizures immediately
Avoid antacids, iron, zinc, multivitamins or sucralfate within 2 hours of the dose
Diabetics: monitor blood sugar; recognize low-sugar symptoms
Limit sun exposure and use sunscreen
Tell your doctor about sudden severe chest/back/abdominal pain
pk: Rapid absorption; therapeutic levels within hours
Store at controlled room temperature per labeling
pearls: Boxed warning: disabling and potentially irreversible tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy and CNS effects can occur together — discontinue at first sign and avoid all fluoroquinolones thereafter
Reserve for uncomplicated UTI, acute bronchitis exacerbation and sinusitis only when no other option exists
Avoid in patients with myasthenia gravis — may cause life-threatening respiratory weakness
Associated with aortic aneurysm/dissection, especially in elderly and those with vascular risk factors
Tendon rupture risk increases with age >60, corticosteroids and organ transplant
Can cause severe hypoglycemia (coma/death) in diabetics on insulin or sulfonylureas
Less divalent-cation chelation than other fluoroquinolones, but still separate from cations by 2 hours
missed: Take as soon as remembered; skip if near the next dose. Do not double up.
overdose: Empty stomach, maintain hydration, supportive care; not efficiently removed by dialysis. Low acute toxicity but observe for CNS effects/seizures.
refs: U.S. FDA label via openFDA / DailyMed
